veranderings.rede: AWS 2017 comma before 'en' joining two clauses that each have their own subject and verb (boom/word, hy/kry); the reviewer may judge the shared fronted 'Tog' makes it optional.

veranderings.voor: Die tweede is 'n gas in die lug met die naam koolstofdioksied.
veranderings.na: Die tweede ding is 'n gas in die lug wat koolstofdioksied genoem word.
veranderings.rede: 'met die naam' is wooden; 'wat ... genoem word' is natural, and 'Die tweede ding' matches 'Die eerste ding' and 'Die derde ding'; the protected word stays.

veranderings.blok: Wat die plant met sy kos doen
veranderings.voor: Die plant maak sy eie kos met hierdie drie dinge saam.
veranderings.na: Met hierdie drie dinge saam maak die plant sy eie kos.
veranderings.rede: A trailing 'saam' after the object reads awkwardly; fronting the phrase is the natural order and links back to the previous block.

veranderings.voor: kos uit die lug en water
veranderings.rede: The article on only one of the two nouns is unbalanced; 'uit lug en water' matches the glossary wording for fotosintese.

veranderings.voor: Sonder kos kan 'n dier nie beweeg nie en ook nie groei nie.
veranderings.na: Sonder kos kan 'n dier nie beweeg of groei nie.
veranderings.rede: The doubled negative construction is clumsy; one negation over 'beweeg of groei' says the same thing more naturally.

veranderings.voor: 'n Leeu is 'n karnivoor en hy jag ander diere vir sy kos.
veranderings.na: 'n Leeu is 'n karnivoor wat ander diere vir sy kos jag.
veranderings.rede: A relative clause is smoother than 'en hy', avoids the missing AWS comma, and parallels the cow and pig sentences ('n Koei is 'n herbivoor wat ...).

vlae.rede: The only verb in a list of nouns (voeding, groei, asemhaling ...); the noun form would be 'voortplanting', but this is a subject term and should be checked against the CAPS list wording rather than changed by a language agent.

vlae.blok: Diere wat plante en diere eet
vlae.teks: 'n Dier wat plante sowel as ander diere eet, staan bekend as 'n omnivoor.
vlae.rede: The herbivoor and karnivoor study sentences repeat the decided glossary wording exactly, but this one says 'ander diere' where the decided omnivoor definition says 'vleis'; not changed because it touches a shared definition.
